Earlier this summer, Apple significantly raised product prices in response to the ongoing global memory crisis. For example, the iPad Air went from $599 to $749, the M5 MacBook Pro went from $1,699 to $1,999, and the Apple TV also went from $129 to $199. The above are just some examples—the key point is that the magnitude of this round of price increases is quite staggering.

This situation inevitably raises the question—will Apple make major improvements to make its products more attractive at the new price points?

Of course, some Apple products are about to undergo major refreshes, with the MacBook Pro and iPad mini being two of them. However, for products that won't see major updates in the short term, I really can't imagine Apple successfully selling "yesterday's technology" at much higher prices while still making consumers feel it's a great deal—especially when compared to current second-hand market prices.

If you could buy an M4 iPad Air for $599 (or even as low as $499) just a few months ago, why would you want to pay $749 today? This argument becomes even more pronounced for higher-priced products.

Some Apple products have gone without major changes for quite a while. The iPad Air has used the same design and features since 2020, only swapping out chips and adding Apple Pencil Pro support; the basic iPad has remained largely the same since 2022; and the iMac has looked pretty much the same since 2021.

Do these products need a redesign? Not necessarily. But I think Apple could do something to make them more attractive at their current price points. For instance, giving the iMac a miniLED display, adding 120Hz refresh rate to the iPad Air, or switching the basic iPad to a fully laminated display.

Compared to price hikes, the upgrades above would cost relatively little, but should make consumers feel better about buying these products at the new prices. On the other hand, Apple might also cut specifications on some products to offset the price increases—for example, the iPhone's storage could once again start at 128GB.

What are your thoughts on Apple's product lineup after the price hikes? Feel free to share your opinions in the comments section.
